messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager fired for gpu-pool-3 (severity: high). Alert: cuda/cuMemAlloc failed -> OOM-ish behavior on nodes [gw-03, gw-07]. Trigger: cuda_alloc_error_rate > 0.05 for 5m. Link: https://pd.company/pagers/INC-6182736455
PagerDuty: Pager INC-6182736455 created, escalation policy: eng-oncall. Primary: Devon, rotations: Chris -> Mariya.
Devon: acked. I'm on it. Starting triage.
Devon: quick checks — `nvidia-smi` on gw-03 shows 100% memory usage on GPU0, process pid 22133 (redwood-runtime). No obvious cuda driver resets.
Devon: past 10m logs from runtime (excerpt):
```
2026-03-15T02:10:12Z runtime: request id=abc123 seq=512 -> kvcache miss
2026-03-15T02:10:13Z runtime: attempting cuMemAlloc(size=4286578688) -> CUDARuntimeError: cuMemAlloc failed (63) out of memory
2026-03-15T02:10:13Z runtime: fallback to smaller model variant v2-quant -> success
2026-03-15T02:12:44Z runtime: repeated cuMemAlloc failures, evicting kvcache keys
```
Devon: looks like sustained allocation growth, maybe a kvcache leak for long-context requests. kv-evictions spiked and then stopped but memory didn't free fast enough.
Chris: @Devon do we have auto-evict policy enabled for this pool? What was the threshold?
Devon: auto-evict = enabled, threshold=0.85. But logs show allocations pushed past 0.95 before evictions kicked in. Might be fragmentation. Also gw-07 shows repeated `cuMemAlloc failed (63)` but restarted worker once and it recovered briefly.
Mariya: @Devon @Chris tagging infra — are these nodes in a dedicated customer pool or shared hosted? I need to know customer impact ASAP.
Devon: Both: gw-03 is in Dedicated cluster for AcmeCorp (reserved), gw-07 is in shared hosted-embedding pool. Early indication: 2 reserved slots affected (Acme), and ~8% increase in tail latency for host-embedding routes.
Chris: Escalate if reserved customer impacted. AcmeCorp SLAs need 99.9% p95. We're looking at p95 degradation to ~1.8s from 0.6s across their pinned model routes.
Devon: mitigation attempts: 1) triggered manual worker restart on gw-03 -> temporarily freed memory but process came back and memory climbed again. 2) attempted `runtime --scale 1` to spawn new process on gw-11 -> new process allocated model successfully but traffic routing still sending some sessions to gw-03 due to sticky routing.
Mariya: do we have a quick workaround? Can we set pool to drain and move traffic?
Devon: yes, I'm going to set pool weight of gw-03 to 0 and enable immediate reroute for in-flight requests (force-failover). Will do in 30s.
Devon: /config route set-weight --pool gpu-pool-3 --node gw-03 0 -> done. Initiating reroute.
Devon: note: reroute reduced new allocations to gw-03, but existing long-lived sessions still hold KV cache. We should consider forcibly terminating a few worker processes to release memory (aggressive).
Chris: before killing, check whether the evictor is stuck due to a pending CUDA kernel. Any `nvidia-smi pmon` info?
Devon: `nvidia-smi pmon -c 1` shows pid 22133 on GPU0 running a long kernel (likely attention computation) for ~4m; it's not releasing because request is huge (seq len ~20480).
Mariya: customer comms: @support-team please prepare a short note to AcmeCorp: "We're mitigating an active GPU memory pressure issue impacting reserved capacity for your cluster. Engineers are rerouting traffic and performing process-level remediation. We'll follow up with timeline and root cause."
Devon: actioning hard-kill of top-2 memory hogs on gw-03 to free space (will attempt graceful SIGTERM first).
Chris: I'll watch for cascade — hard-kill could drop some in-flight requests and increase error rates; coordinate with support for error windows.
Devon: executed `pkill -TERM -P 22133` then after 10s `pkill -KILL -P 22133`. Freed ~36GB on GPU0.
Devon: new `nvidia-smi` shows memory dropped to 18% on gw-03. Routing now stable.
PagerDuty: INC-6182736455 acknowledged by Devon at 2026-03-15T02:18:05Z.
Mariya: good work. Can you collect heap/kvcache stats and open a debug trace for pid 22133 (pre-kill) so research can look at why kvcache didn't evict properly?
Devon: saved trace: `/var/log/runtime/traces/trace-6182736455.tar.gz` and uploaded to share: https://files.company/trace-6182736455. kvcache had ~1.2M keys and top key was 1.1GB. Looks like a single request with a huge prefix caused unbounded growth.
Chris: adding temporary guard: set per-request prefix limit to 1M tokens for gpu-pool-3 and a hard allocation cap of 10GB per worker to avoid single-request OOM.
Devon: applied: `/config runtime set --pool gpu-pool-3 --prefill-limit 1000000 --worker-max-gpu 10G` -> confirmed.
Mariya: customer impact summary for support: "AcmeCorp experienced degraded p95 for model-serving for ~12 minutes. Some in-flight requests returned 502 during hard-kill window (~30s). No data exfiltration. Dedicated cluster availability returned to SLA after reroute and worker restarts. Investigating kvcache leak for root cause."
Chris: follow-ups: 1) postmortem if root cause confirmed as request-level (huge prefix) abuse or bug in kvcache accounting. 2) add alert to detect single-request key-size > 500MB. 3) consider fragmentation mitigation: periodic worker restart on >90% GPU sustained.
Devon: handing off to Mariya for long-term remediation + customer comms. I'll stay on for any needed logs.
Mariya: taking over. I've created GH issue: redwood/runtime#4521 with attached traces and initial notes. Assigning to runtime team and marking P1.
Mariya: also created support ticket SUP-8842 for AcmeCorp with the incident summary and timeline.
Chris: thanks team. Closing pager once follow-ups are tracked.
PagerDuty: Pager INC-6182736455 resolved by Mariya at 2026-03-15T02:42:35Z (duration ~24m).
Devon: quick ops note: consider lowering auto-evict threshold to 0.7 and enabling preemptive kv-shrink on high-long-tail models.
Mariya: agreed. I'll schedule a config rollout and include a changelog entry.
Devon: thanks all :thumbsup:
